## How to work

This practice contains 11 core tasks followed by two optional tasks. Each task is independent. Write R code that saves the requested answer as `result`.

On Stepik, the input variables are prepared automatically and your saved result is checked automatically. **Here you need to check your answers by yourself.**

## 1. Solution concentration

A solution contains a known amount of a dissolved substance. Calculate its concentration in mg/L and save it as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `mass_mg` -- mass of the dissolved substance in milligrams
- `volume_ml` -- volume of the solution in millilitres

```{r}
mass_mg <- 30
volume_ml <- 250

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
120
```

## 2. A sequence with a fixed step

Create a numeric vector that starts at `start` and increases by `step` without exceeding `end`. Include `end` if the sequence reaches it. Save the vector as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `start` -- first value
- `end` -- upper limit, at least `start`
- `step` -- positive increment between values

```{r}
start <- 2
end <- 12
step <- 3

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
2 5 8 11
```

## 3. Treatment and control groups

An experiment has a treatment group and a control group. Make a character vector with one label per participant. Put all the `"treatment"` labels first, followed by the `"control"` labels. Save the vector as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `n_treatment` -- number of participants in the treatment group
- `n_control` -- number of participants in the control group

```{r}
n_treatment <- 3
n_control <- 2

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
treatment treatment treatment control control
```

## 4. A faulty reading

One reading was recorded incorrectly, and you know its position. Remove that entry, keep the other readings in their original order, and save the vector as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `readings` -- numeric vector of recorded measurements
- `faulty_position` -- position of the faulty reading, counting from 1

```{r}
readings <- c(110, 95, 103, 95, 112)
faulty_position <- 2

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
110 103 95 112
```

## 5. Mass without the container

Each sample was weighed in a container. Subtract the mass of its empty container to find the mass of each sample. Save the resulting vector as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `gross_g` -- total masses of the samples with their containers, in grams
- `container_g` -- masses of the empty containers in the same order, in grams

```{r}
gross_g <- c(28, 31, 25)
container_g <- c(8, 10, 9)

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
20 21 16
```

## 6. Samples that pass quality control

A lab accepts samples whose signals fall within a specified range. Find the IDs of samples with signals from `lower` to `upper`, including both limits. Keep their original order and save the vector as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `sample_id` -- character vector of sample IDs
- `signal` -- numeric vector of signals in the same order
- `lower` -- minimum acceptable signal
- `upper` -- maximum acceptable signal

```{r}
sample_id <- c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5")
signal <- c(105, 95, 92, 115, 110)
lower <- 95
upper <- 110

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
S1 S2 S5
```

## 7. Readings above the mean

A lab recorded several readings. Calculate their mean and count how many readings are strictly above it. Save the count as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `signal` -- numeric vector of recorded readings

```{r}
signal <- c(4, 6, 8, 22)

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
1
```

## 8. Create and filter a data frame

Use the sample data from the quality-control task to create a data frame with columns `id` and `signal`. Keep only rows whose signal is from `lower` to `upper`, including both limits. Keep the original row order and save the filtered data frame as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `sample_id` -- character vector of sample IDs
- `signal` -- numeric vector of signals in the same order
- `lower` -- minimum acceptable signal
- `upper` -- maximum acceptable signal

```{r}
sample_id <- c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5")
signal <- c(105, 95, 92, 115, 110)
lower <- 95
upper <- 110

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
id signal
1 S1    105
2 S2     95
3 S5    110
```

## 9. Add a plant mass gain column

The same plants were weighed at the start and end of an experiment. Calculate the final mass minus the initial mass for each plant. Add the values as a new column named `gain_g` and save the full data frame as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `plants` -- data frame with one row per plant and columns `id`, `start_g`, and `end_g`. Both masses are in grams

```{r}
plants <- data.frame(
  id = c("P1", "P2", "P3", "P4"),
  start_g = c(12, 10, 14, 11),
  end_g = c(16, 9, 16, 11)
)

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
id start_g end_g gain_g
1 P1      12    16      4
2 P2      10     9     -1
3 P3      14    16      2
4 P4      11    11      0
```

## 10. Count samples from selected channels

A lab measured samples on several channels. Count the samples from the selected channels whose signal is at least `min_signal`. Save the count as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `samples` -- data frame with one row per sample and columns `id`, `channel`, and `signal`
- `selected_channels` -- character vector of channels to include
- `min_signal` -- minimum signal to include

```{r}
samples <- data.frame(
  id = c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4", "S5", "S6"),
  channel = c("A", "B", "C", "A", "B", "C"),
  signal = c(103, 112, 110, 95, 88, 99)
)
selected_channels <- c("A", "C")
min_signal <- 99

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
3
```

## 11. Mean signal on one channel

A lab wants to summarise readings from a single channel. Keep samples on the target channel with signals from `lower` to `upper`, including both limits. Calculate their mean signal to two decimal places and save it as `result`. At least one sample meets the conditions.

**Variables already available in R**

- `samples` -- data frame with one row per sample and columns `channel` and `signal`
- `target_channel` -- channel to analyse
- `lower` -- minimum signal to include
- `upper` -- maximum signal to include

Hint

Look up `?round` in R.

```{r}
samples <- data.frame(
  channel = c("A", "B", "A", "A", "B", "A"),
  signal = c(95, 100, 110, 105, 98, 115)
)
target_channel <- "A"
lower <- 95
upper <- 110

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
103.33
```

## 12. Optional practice with ifelse()

A reading passes quality control if it reaches the threshold. Use `ifelse()` to label each reading `"pass"` or `"fail"`. Keep the original order and save the character vector as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `signal` -- numeric vector of readings
- `threshold` -- smallest reading that passes

Hint

`ifelse(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)` chooses a value for each element of a logical vector. For example, `ifelse(c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE), "yes", "no")` returns `c("yes", "no", "yes")`.

```{r}
signal <- c(105, 95, 92, 115)
threshold <- 95

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
pass pass fail pass
```

## 13. Optional practice with which()

A lab keeps sample IDs and signals in separate components of a list. Use `which()` to find the position of the target ID, then use that position to get its signal. Save the signal as `result`.

**Variables already available in R**

- `run` -- list with `id` and `signal` vectors in the same order
- `target_id` -- sample ID to look up, appearing exactly once in `run$id`

Hint

`which(c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))` returns `2`. Compare `run$id` with `target_id` to create a logical vector. Use the position returned by `which()` to select an element of `run$signal`.

```{r}
run <- list(
  id = c("S1", "S2", "S3", "S4"),
  signal = c(105, 95, 92, 115)
)
target_id <- "S3"

# Write your solution here.
# result <- ...
```

**Example result**

``` text
92
```
